title: Successful logins must not consume password-failure budget
body: The original guard counted all login POSTs toward five attempts per fifteen minutes. Browser verification and smoke tests used the shared proxy identity and exhausted the allowance with successful logins, making the owner's unchanged password return 429. Do not trust arbitrary forwarded-IP headers to work around this.
resolution: Count only incorrect passwords under a Postgres row lock, reset failures on successful login, preserve the five-failure lockout with Retry-After, and retain a separate sixty-request-per-minute cap. Clear the pre-fix login failure bucket during this rollout. Regression tests cover repeated success, resetting failures, concurrent attempts and expiry.

title: Read autofilled passwords from native fields and verify sessions
body: A no-error login report exposed two reproducible silent paths: password-manager autofill without React change events left the button disabled and submit handler reading empty state; successful POST login followed by unauthenticated GET session silently reset the form. Ordinary Playwright fill() and cookie-accepting smoke checks missed both. The user's precise browser condition was not observed directly.
resolution: Use an uncontrolled native password field and FormData at submit, disable submission only while busy, return an explicit boolean from session verification, and show an actionable error if the session is missing. Keep the field on failure. Guard button and Enter autofill and discarded-session cases in both Chrome and WebKit.

title: Distinguish missing cookies from parser and session failures
body: SimpleCookie can reject the entire Cookie header when an unrelated preceding cookie contains raw JSON, and converting ASGI headers to a dict loses repeated Cookie fields. Both failures reproduce in backend tests. However, a public-browser test through boxd already accepted that synthetic cookie before the parser fix, so this was not established as the owner's cause. Successful-password session failures need transport diagnostics rather than another assumption about the password or rate limit.
resolution: Combine every Cookie field and use Starlette's browser-tolerant cookie_parser; still validate the opaque session token against Postgres. Return cookie_received from session verification and show COOKIE_MISSING versus COOKIE_REJECTED in login errors. Production logs record session status only, never cookie values. Wait for the owner's next attempt to identify their remaining failure.
